commits.headline: ci: the SDK template's workflow, with SHA256SUMS and published releases
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The same file as the SDK's template (1.0.2): Windows through MSVC
with Ninja (the Visual Studio 2022 generator found no instance on
windows-latest), Ninja from pip everywhere, SHA256SUMS over every
archive, and a tag v<version> or <id>-v<version> publishing the
release the launcher installs from. fetch_sdk.py is the template's,
which can also take a release's hash on the first fetch.

commits.headline: build: pin the mod SDK 1.0.2; install from the launcher by link
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
sdk.lock pins the SDK 1.0.2 release and its SHA-256. README: adding
the mods by pasting the repository's address in the launcher, and
releasing with a tag. Built and tested against it on macOS.

commits.headline: fix: LF line endings on every system, as the SDK template's
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The Windows build's README came out CRLF and the merge refused to
join its archive with the others'.

commits.headline: feat(item-randomizer): a seeded item randomizer with logic, on OpenRAC's item hook points
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
Shuffles the gadgets and weapons NPCs and pickups give, the vendor's
weapons, the gold bolts and the infobots' coordinates. The locations come
from the decompilation (each GiveItem and UnlockPlanet and the test around
it, the gold bolt's update, the vendor's stock) and the PAL disc's level
data; each says what it needs. An assumed fill places the rewards that open
the way where they can be had without them, and every placement is played
through before it is used. Seed codes carry the settings…

commits.headline: docs(item-randomizer): how to play it, and how it works
commits.author: Veradictus

commits.headline: feat(lock-strafe): the mod in C++ on the SDK's openrac/mod.hpp
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
lock_strafe.cpp in place of lock_strafe.c, the reference C++ mod: the
six hook points taken with lambdas that go on to their originals,
Hero_TurnToHeading's original called from the standing turn through
mod.original<>(), refusals (another game, an unknown disc, a missing
game function or hook point) thrown as openrac::Error, typed settings,
game memory through openrac::Memory and the swing's heading on the
game's stack through openrac::StackFrame. strafe.h's decision and
discs.h's tables are…

commits.headline: test(lock-strafe): the load test checks the interface the SDK names
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The query's version against OPENRAC_MOD_API_MAJOR and _MINOR of the
SDK it was built with, rather than 1.0 written in, so the test holds
when the SDK's interface moves to 1.1.

commits.headline: docs(lock-strafe): the mod is C++ now
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The README names lock_strafe.cpp and a C++17 compiler, and the mod's
history says it moved from C on the interface's table to the SDK's C++
layer; strafe.h's comments name lock_strafe.cpp.

commits.headline: feat(button-swap): a script mod that swaps two buttons
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The first script mod and the example of them (OpenRAC's
docs/port/MODS.md, section 11): Luau, interface 1.1, PAL and NTSC-U,
one openrac.on_pad callback that trades two buttons' bits in the pad
report's button word and their pressure bytes before the game reads
it: Cross and Square (the default), Circle and Triangle, or L1 and R1,
the setting pair. The README gives the report's layout as the port's
pad library writes it (port/game/common/lib/pad.c).

Checked and packaged with the SDK's…

commits.headline: ci: the SDK template's workflow, which packages script mods
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The same file as the SDK's template again: a detect job finds the
native mods (the top CMakeLists.txt) and the script mods (manifests
with type script, one folder deep), the script mods are packaged with
no build as <id>-<version>.zip, and they join SHA256SUMS and the
tag's release beside the native mods' archives.

commits.headline: docs: native and script mods, and button-swap
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The two kinds of mod, what the launcher says of each, button-swap in
the list, packaging a script mod, and adding one from the SDK's
script template.

commits.headline: test(lock-strafe): the load test's host takes hook points by their ids
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The SDK's C++ layer asks for a hook point by its permanent id
(rac1.player.turn_to_heading) since SDK 1.1.0; the test's host resolves
the ids to the names as the port's loader does.

commits.headline: fix(lock-strafe): built for the mod interface 1.1
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
The SDK 1.1 header reports interface 1.1, and the port checks the
manifest against the library's own answer.

commits.headline: build: pin the mod SDK 1.1.0; link the modding guides
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
sdk.lock pins the SDK 1.1.0 release (the C++ layer, script mods) and
its SHA-256; the README links the SDK's guides for making a mod.

commits.headline: fix(item-randomizer): built for the mod interface 1.1
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
With the SDK pinned at 1.1.0 the library's OPENRAC_MOD_DEFINE reports
interface 1.1, and the port refuses a manifest that says otherwise.

commits.headline: build: pin the mod SDK 1.1.1, whose workflow releases one mod per tag
commits.author: Veradictus
commits.body:
A tag <id>-v<version> now publishes that mod's archives alone, so the
mods here are released apart (lock-strafe-v1.0.0, button-swap-v1.0.0).
